  "stdout": "159:| [`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) | On a pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag: checks the tag, creates a draft GitHub Release, and moves the major tag. See [Releases](#releases) |
160-
161:## Releases
162-
163:A release is a pull request that changes the version, then a tag on its merge commit. [`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) does the rest. Users refer to the action by its major tag, such as `cv/pi-action@v2`.
164-
165-1. Make a branch from `main`, and set the version. `npm version` changes `package.json` and `package-lock.json`:
166-
--
168:   git switch -c chore/release-X.Y.Z main
169-   npm version X.Y.Z --no-git-tag-version
170:   git commit -am "chore: release X.Y.Z"
171:   git push -u origin chore/release-X.Y.Z
172-   ```
173-
174:2. Open a pull request with the title `chore: release X.Y.Z`. Write the notes in a `## Release notes` section of its description, in the [release notes format](#release-notes).
175-3. When CI passes, squash-merge the pull request.
176-4. Tag the merge commit on `main` with an annotated tag, and push the tag:
177-
--
184:5. `release.yml` makes sure that the tag agrees with `package.json` and is on `main`, and runs `npm run check`. Then it creates a draft GitHub Release with the `## Release notes` section, and moves the major tag (`vN`) to the commit. It does not move the major tag back for a tag that is earlier than the latest one.
185:6. Review the draft in [Releases](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/releases), and publish it.
186-
187:### Release notes
188-
189-Write the notes for users. Copy this structure:
190-
--
202:- Use full links to the docs of the tag (`blob/vX.Y.Z/...`), so that the links stay correct after later releases.
203:- Do not add the **Full Changelog** link. `release.yml` adds it.
204-
205-## Pull requests
206-
